description: Two big eyes in a wobble of pond water. Corner it and it bursts into spray, then gathers itself back up.
lore: This is the first of them most new stars meet, and the one that has to be explained twice. Nothing fell to make it. No creature drowned in that water and came back small and round; there was never anybody in there at all. A low wet place got remembered by a great many people and walked past by none of them for a long while, and the remembering pooled the way water pools, and one morning it had a face on it.

Fight one and it bursts. It is alarming exactly once. The whole thing comes apart into spray, sits a moment as a flat wet patch on the ground, and is a blob again before you have finished deciding how you feel about it. Nothing you do to it lands the way it looks like it lands, because there is nothing in it for anything to land on.

People who sort creatures for a living get one question into the usual list and stop. What has it lost, they ask — and the question has nowhere to go, because there was never anything in it to be losing. It holds together for exactly as long as the remembering it condensed out of stays pooled where it is, and when that goes elsewhere it comes apart. Whether that is an ending, and whose, gets argued at fires and settles nothing.

It is water gathered round stones and it leaves both. There is a smooth grey-blue river stone it carries about the way it carries everything, for no reason it could give; the frogs down there keep one too, which is either evidence of something or the least interesting coincidence in the valley. Under that is the hard piece — dull brown plates veined with copper, egg-sized, warm, and much heavier in the palm than the whole creature looked from ten paces. Worked into armour it makes a person very difficult to shift, and that is the one true thing about a puddle, kept. A puddle is not brave and it is not stubborn. It simply cannot be pushed off its own low place, and it is back in it whatever the weather does, and it will still be there when everything that used to walk past it has gone.
